name: Four-choice reversal digging task

fields.label: Strain
fields.Description: Strain of the mouse, e.g. C57BL/6.

fields.label: Genotype
fields.Description: Genotype: WT, HET or KO, for example.

fields.label: Experiment Cohort
fields.Description: Cohort the mouse was run in, e.g. MAABCD_2026.

fields.label: Adversity Condition
fields.Description: Model of adversity or stress tested, e.g. Food Insecurity.

fields.label: Adversity Age Range (PXX-XX)
fields.Description: Postnatal age range of the adversity, e.g. P21-40.

fields.label: Bred On Site or Shipped
fields.Description: Whether the mouse was bred on site or shipped.

fields.label: # Of Mice In Homecage At Testing
fields.Description: Number of mice in the homecage at testing.

phenotype.name: weight
phenotype.description: Weight tracking from the WEIGHT tab of the 4C Digging Reversal Reporting Sheet, one group of columns per experimental day.

fields.label: Stage
fields.Description: Stage of the protocol that day.

fields.label: % from baseline
fields.Description: That day's weight divided by the Day 1 reference ad libitum weight.

time_to_eat_nw_1.Description: Time the mouse took to start eating the plain pellet in the northwest quadrant (1).

time_to_eat_ne_2.Description: Time the mouse took to start eating the plain pellet in the northeast quadrant (2).

time_to_eat_sw_3.Description: Time the mouse took to start eating the plain pellet in the southwest quadrant (3).

time_to_eat_se_4.Description: Time the mouse took to start eating the plain pellet in the southeast quadrant (4).

bedding_level.Description: Amount of shavings in the ramekin; it increases with each shaping trial.

ramekin_position.Description: Quadrant the ramekin was placed in: NW, NE, SW or SE.

time_to_dig_s.Description: Time until the mouse purposefully touched the pellet or the shavings.

time_to_eat_s.Description: Time until the mouse started eating the pellet.

ramekin_order.Description: Order of the four odor ramekins by position (northwest, northeast, southwest, southeast), written as the odor letters A to D listed at the top of the sheet.

correct.Description: Whether the choice was the rewarded odor.

latency_s.Description: Time the mouse took to dig, in seconds (written as mm:ss on the testing sheet and converted for the reporting sheet).

entry_sequence.Description: Order in which the quadrants were entered: 1 = northwest, 2 = northeast, 3 = southwest, 4 = southeast.

odor_sequences.Description: The odor of each quadrant entered, in order: the entry sequence read through the ramekin order.

error_type.Description: Kind of error made in the reversal stage; the protocol's types are Reversal, Perseverative, Regressive, Novel and Irrelevant.

notes.Description: Free-text notes from the experimenter: grooming, jumping, climbing, sleeping or chewing for 5 seconds (tick marks count repeats), the time to dig and time to eat of a reminder trial after two omissions, and a 15-minute break.

description: In the four choice reversal digging task mice must identify the single rewarded option and update their choice when a previously unrewarded option becomes rewarded. The reversal phase in this task is sensitive to orbitofrontal and dorsomedial prefrontal cortex function and the 2-day version used here provides a metric of recall on the 2nd day of testing before reversal.

name: ASST digging task
description: The attentional set-shifting task (ASST) is a rodent analogue of the Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Battery (CANTAB) IED task. It assesses the ability to shift attention between perceptual dimensions of compound stimuli. The task requires animals to learn sequential discriminations, measuring the cost of shifting attention from one perceptual dimension to another.
references: Ma, S., Wang, K. H., & Zuo, Y. (2026). Targeting insulo-frontal pathway to reduce stress-evoked cognitive rigidity. Nature Communications.

name: Two arm bandit task
description: The two-armed bandit task is a classic paradigm in behavioral neuroscience used to study decision-making under uncertainty. In this task, participants are presented with two options, each associated with a different probability of reward. By repeatedly choosing between the two options, participants learn to exploit the option with the higher reward probability while also exploring the other option to ensure that they are not missing out on a potentially better source of reward. This task has been used to investigate the neural mechanisms underlying reinforcement learning, exploration-exploitation trade-offs, and the role of different brain regions in decision-making.
